$why: English overlay for the AI museum timeline. The canon pack (public/proto/data/screens/museum.json) is a pixel contract and stays Korean-only; this file is the separate translation layer, keyed by canon event id. An id absent here falls back to Korean AND keeps its Korean language tag, so a partly translated timeline never tells assistive technology the wrong language. Adding an id here is what makes that node English.
$notTheLocaleBundle: This deliberately does NOT live in locales/en/. check-i18n-keys.ts requires every namespace present in locales/en/ to exist in all five locale folders, so a namespace here would demand es/pt/id translations of 11,643 Korean characters AND a Korean copy that would drift from the canon it was copied out of. Measured, not assumed: scripts/check-i18n-keys.ts:53-74.

w_ww2.title: World War II
w_ww2.body: The enormous demand for codebreaking gave birth to the first electronic computers. Alan Turing's Bombe, Colossus, and the explosion of computing that led to ENIAC in 1945 laid the ground for a later question: can a machine think?
w_ww2.long: The codebreaking work at Bletchley Park was a secret computing project on a national scale. Turing's Bombe broke Enigma and Colossus broke the Lorenz cipher, proving for the first time what electronic computation could do.
w_ww2.cause: The war made calculations no human could finish an urgent necessity.
w_ww2.effect: It left behind both the electronic computer and the question of the thinking machine.

w_sputnik.title: The Sputnik shock
w_sputnik.sub: The Cold War pours money into science
w_sputnik.body: The Soviet satellite launch sent the United States into a huge scientific investment. That money funded computing and AI research at universities and laboratories, and led shortly afterward to the Dartmouth workshop.
w_sputnik.long: The first Soviet satellite launch in 1957 hit the United States as evidence it was falling behind. NASA and ARPA were founded the following year, and national money flowed into basic research.
w_sputnik.cause: Cold War rivalry turned science into a security question.
w_sputnik.effect: That funding was what first fed computing and AI research at universities.

w_moon.title: Apollo 11
w_moon.sub: A computer takes people to the Moon
w_moon.body: The Apollo Guidance Computer landed humans on the Moon. The idea that a small computer could help make life-or-death judgments began to settle into public trust.
w_moon.long: The Apollo Guidance Computer controlled a Moon landing with about 32 kg of hardware and tens of kilobytes of memory. It was the first time humanity traded its lives on a small machine's real-time judgment.
w_moon.cause: The space race forced the development of small, highly reliable computers.
w_moon.effect: A social instinct took root: a computer's judgment can be trusted.

w_intel.title: Intel 4004
w_intel.sub: A computer on a single chip
w_intel.body: The first commercial microprocessor arrived. Computation that grew cheaper and faster along Moore's law laid the ground that would later make AI practical.
w_intel.long: The Intel 4004 put 2,300 transistors on one chip as the first commercial microprocessor. Computation then grew cheaper and faster every year, exactly as Moore's law described.
w_intel.cause: Integration technology made one chip equal to one computer.
w_intel.effect: Cheap computation became the physical basis of GPU deep learning later on.

w_www.title: The World Wide Web
w_www.sub: An ocean of data opens up
w_www.body: Tim Berners-Lee released the Web, and the human record exploded into digital form. That vast body of data would later feed deep learning and the large language models.
w_www.long: In 1991 Tim Berners-Lee published the first web page at CERN, opening an age in which anyone could link information to anything else. The human record began to grow explosively.
w_www.cause: The internet needed a document standard anyone could write for.
w_www.effect: That ocean of data became the fuel for deep learning and LLMs.

w_dotcom.title: The dot-com bubble
w_dotcom.body: Overheated expectations about the internet burst. The gap between a technology's promise and its reality — later a mirror for looking at the AI boom.
w_dotcom.long: The dot-com bubble was froth built by capital that overestimated the internet's potential. The Nasdaq fell sharply from its peak in 2000, but the firms and infrastructure that survived became the ground for the next decade.
w_dotcom.cause: Irrational enthusiasm for a new technology inflated prices.
w_dotcom.effect: "Promise and bubble" is the mirror we hold up to today's AI boom.

w_iphone.title: The iPhone arrives
w_iphone.body: The smartphone changed daily life. Data made by billions of cameras, sensors, and touches became the fuel for mobile AI and deep learning.
w_iphone.long: The 2007 iPhone put multi-touch, apps, and an always-on internet in one hand. Behavioural data from billions of cameras and sensors became the fuel for mobile AI.
w_iphone.cause: Phones, the internet, and touch were ready to converge into one device.
w_iphone.effect: Personal data exploded, and recommendation and recognition AI entered daily life.

w_gfc.title: The global financial crisis
w_gfc.body: The collapse of Lehman Brothers shook the world economy. Demand exploded afterwards for managing risk with data and algorithms across finance and industry.
w_gfc.long: The 2008 bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers brought global finance to a halt. Industry then tried to read risk through data and models, and demand for quantitative decision-making exploded.
w_gfc.cause: Systemic risk nobody could see went off all at once.
w_gfc.effect: Demand grew for managing risk with data and algorithms.

w_covid.title: The COVID-19 pandemic
w_covid.body: Remote work and contact-free life became ordinary, pulling digital transformation forward by years. Demand for cloud, video, and automation exploded, and AI tools moved quickly into work and life.
refs: Remote work and video calls spread
w_covid.long: The pandemic moved work, education, and healthcare online overnight. Demand for cloud, video, and automation exploded, and people finished getting ready to accept AI tools quickly.
w_covid.cause: Physical distance pushed every activity online.
w_covid.effect: That digital familiarity became the ground for the ChatGPT explosion two years later.

w_genai.title: The generative AI boom
w_genai.body: AI that makes images and text became the subject of conversation everywhere. Hope and anxiety about creation, education, and work broke out at the same time.
w_genai.long: DALL·E 2, Midjourney, and Stable Diffusion arrived in quick succession in 2022, and anyone could make an image from one line of text. Hope and anxiety about creative work and labour broke out together.
w_genai.cause: Diffusion models and large-scale data made generation something everyone could do.
w_genai.effect: AI moved out of the lab and became a language of popular culture.

w_regul.title: AI regulation and everyday use
w_regul.body: Debate over copyright, jobs, and safety began in earnest, and governments started building frameworks for regulating AI. AI became a question of social institutions, not only of technology.
w_regul.long: In 2024 the EU passed the AI Act, the first comprehensive AI law anywhere. Debate over copyright, jobs, and safety was written into institutions, and AI became a question of social norms rather than technology alone.
w_regul.cause: Fast adoption exposed the risk of having no rules.
w_regul.effect: Society began asking how it wants to live alongside AI.

a_turing.title: The Turing test
a_turing.sub: The question of a thinking machine
a_turing.body: Alan Turing turned "can a machine think?" into a question that could be measured. If conversation alone cannot tell a person from a machine, his proposal was, call that intelligence.
a_turing.long: Turing replaced the vague question of whether a machine thinks with a testable game: can it be told apart from a person in conversation? That imitation game is still the starting line for the argument about intelligence.
a_turing.cause: Wartime computing experience made machine intelligence a serious question.
a_turing.effect: Six years later, Dartmouth launched a field called AI.

a_dartmouth.title: The Dartmouth workshop
a_dartmouth.body: A summer workshop gave the name "artificial intelligence" to the field for the first time. The official moment it set out as a discipline of its own.
a_dartmouth.long: At the Dartmouth workshop in the summer of 1956, McCarthy, Minsky, Shannon and others gathered under the banner of a new term: artificial intelligence. It was a field's birth certificate.
a_dartmouth.cause: Turing's question needed a research community to answer it.
a_dartmouth.effect: Early neural network work, the perceptron among it, poured out.

a_perceptron.title: The perceptron
a_perceptron.sub: The seed of the neural network
a_perceptron.body: Rosenblatt's perceptron was the first model to learn by imitating the neurons of the brain. The first spark of the connectionism that leads to today's deep learning.
a_perceptron.long: Rosenblatt's perceptron was the first artificial neuron that weighted its inputs and adjusted those weights itself. It is the first spark of the connectionism that runs to today's deep learning.
a_perceptron.cause: After Dartmouth, the idea of copying the brain took concrete form.
a_perceptron.effect: Its limits soon became the pretext for the first AI winter.

a_winter.title: The first AI winter
a_winter.body: The perceptron's limit (the XOR problem) was proved mathematically, and neural network research entered a long stagnation. Rule-based symbolic AI became the mainstream for a while.
a_winter.long: When Minsky and Papert proved that a single-layer perceptron could not even solve XOR, funding for neural network research dried up. Rule-based symbolic AI held the mainstream for a while afterwards.
a_winter.cause: Early expectations ran into a technical wall.
a_winter.effect: Seventeen years later backpropagation broke through that wall and woke the field.

a_backprop.title: Backpropagation
a_backprop.body: Backpropagation, which corrects weights by running the error backwards, made multi-layer networks trainable. The decisive key to waking neural networks from the first winter.
a_backprop.long: In 1986 Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams popularised backpropagation and opened the way to training multi-layer networks. Sending the error backwards to correct the weights became deep learning's engine.
a_backprop.cause: A way to learn deeply enough to clear the XOR barrier was badly needed.
a_backprop.effect: Neural networks revived, leading to the deep learning reignition of 2006.

a_deepblue.title: Deep Blue
a_deepblue.body: IBM's Deep Blue beat world chess champion Garry Kasparov. A symbolic moment: in one domain, a machine had passed the best human.
a_deepblue.long: In 1997 IBM's Deep Blue read roughly 200 million positions a second and defeated the chess champion Garry Kasparov. In a world of fixed rules, it is the symbol of a machine first passing the best human.
a_deepblue.cause: Faster computation let raw search overwhelm a human.
a_deepblue.effect: The next challenge was Go, whose intuition no rule could reach.

a_dl2006.title: Deep learning reignites
a_dl2006.body: Hinton reopened the path to training deep neural networks effectively. The word "deep learning" began to be used in earnest.
refs: A Fast Learning Algorithm for Deep Belief Nets
a_dl2006.long: In 2006 Hinton trained deep networks stably with layer-by-layer pre-training, and the term deep learning took hold. With data and computation now ripe, an old idea stood on the edge of an explosion.
a_dl2006.cause: Backpropagation, data, and hardware met at one moment.
a_dl2006.effect: Six years later AlexNet proved that potential to everyone.

a_alexnet.title: AlexNet
a_alexnet.body: A deep neural network won the ImageNet recognition contest by an overwhelming margin. The watershed that announced the era of deep learning trained on GPUs.
a_alexnet.long: In 2012 AlexNet, a deep CNN trained on GPUs, cut the ImageNet error rate sharply in a single step. It is the watershed at which deep learning left academia and became an industrial standard.
a_alexnet.effect: Everyone moved to deep learning, and it spread to speech, translation, and Go.

a_alphago.title: AlphaGo
a_alphago.body: AlphaGo beat the top Go player Lee Sedol 4-1. The moment learning crossed even into intuition, the territory said to be beyond calculation.
refs: DeepMind · the five games with Lee Sedol
a_alphago.long: In 2016 AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol 4-1 using policy and value networks trained through self-play. Learning had crossed into the intuition of Go, a game said to hold more possibilities than there are atoms in the universe.
a_alphago.cause: Deep learning plus reinforcement learning made intuition tractable.
a_alphago.effect: AI's possibilities were imprinted on the public imagination.

a_transformer.title: The Transformer
a_transformer.body: "Attention is all you need" — a structure that takes in the whole context at once. The design that became the skeleton of every large language model today.
a_transformer.long: Google's 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need" proposed an attention structure that reads the whole context in one pass, without recurrence. Parallel training became easy, and the path to making models enormous opened.
a_transformer.cause: A faster structure for handling long context was needed.
a_transformer.effect: It became the foundation of GPT, BERT, and every large language model.

a_gpt3.title: GPT-3
a_gpt3.sub: Bigger turns out to be smarter
a_gpt3.body: 175 billion parameters. Simply making the model larger turned out to make new abilities emerge.
a_gpt3.long: GPT-3 in 2020 had 175 billion parameters and could solve a new task after seeing only a few examples. Scaling laws showed that ability emerges from size alone.
a_gpt3.cause: The Transformer made "bigger" a realistic thing to try.
a_gpt3.effect: On that foundation, ChatGPT reached the public.

a_chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
a_chatgpt.body: A conversational AI reached 100 million users in two months. The moment AI stopped being an expert's tool and became an everyday language.
a_chatgpt.long: ChatGPT, released in November 2022, used reinforcement learning from human feedback to smooth out conversation and reached 100 million users in two months. AI stopped being an expert's tool and became an everyday language.
a_chatgpt.cause: GPT-3's power gained an interface: conversation.
a_chatgpt.effect: Everyone used AI, and the door to the age of agents opened.

a_agent.title: The age of agents
a_agent.sub: AI that works on its own
a_agent.body: Models picked up tools (RAG, tool use), several AIs began working together, and given only a goal they started planning and acting for themselves. From AI that answers to AI that works.
a_agent.long: Models picked up tools — search, code, RAG — several AIs began working together, and given only a goal they started planning and acting for themselves. The centre of gravity moved from AI that answers to AI that works.
a_agent.cause: A model smart enough was given hands to act with.
a_agent.effect: Next comes a personal AI that understands you and works alongside you.

a_2ndb.title: The second brain
a_2ndb.body: Past an AI that knows the world, to an AI that knows you. A place that grows from your own record and looks for your North Star with you — where SecondB stands.
a_2ndb.long: Past an AI that knows the world, to an AI that knows you. A second brain that draws your scattered records together, looks for meaning with you, and moves toward a North Star that is yours — where SecondB stands.
facts: A North Star of your own
a_2ndb.cause: Agent technology made an AI for one person possible.
a_2ndb.effect: Each of your days grows the second brain.

w_transistor.title: The transistor
w_transistor.body: Bell Labs invented the transistor to replace the vacuum tube. A small, cheap switch became the basic part of every digital device.
w_transistor.long: Smaller and steadier than a vacuum tube, the transistor shrank the computer from the size of a room to the size of a palm. It is the physical starting point of every chip and every calculation.
facts: The seed of the integrated circuit
w_transistor.cause: The heat and failure rate of vacuum tubes demanded a better switch.
w_transistor.effect: Twenty-four years later it bore fruit as the Intel 4004 microprocessor.

w_arpanet.title: ARPANET
w_arpanet.sub: A network takes its first breath
w_arpanet.body: ARPA, in the US Department of Defense, brought up ARPANET to link computers together. Packet switching would grow into the internet.
w_arpanet.long: The first message passed between UCLA and Stanford in 1969. That distributed packet-switching design is the direct ancestor of today's internet.
w_arpanet.cause: The Cold War needed a communications network that would not go down.
w_arpanet.effect: Twenty-two years later, the World Wide Web opened on top of it.

w_google.title: Google Search
w_google.body: Google arrived and ranked the Web with PageRank. A vast body of information became knowledge you could actually find.
w_google.long: PageRank read a link as a vote of trust and changed the quality of search. It sorted the Web's exploding data into something a person could handle.
w_google.cause: The Web grew so large that ordering it became the new problem.
w_google.effect: The companies that handled data became the leading players in AI.

w_bigdata.title: Big data and the cloud
w_bigdata.body: Smartphones, social media, and the cloud made data explode. Called the new oil, that data fed deep learning.
w_bigdata.long: Social media, mobile, and cheap cloud storage met, and data grew exponentially. That abundance of training material became the fuel for the deep learning explosion.
w_bigdata.cause: After the iPhone, everyone was pouring out data.
w_bigdata.effect: Data and GPUs meshed and made AlexNet's leap possible.

a_eliza.title: ELIZA
a_eliza.body: Weizenbaum's ELIZA imitated a counsellor and held conversations with people. The rules were simple, and people opened their hearts to the machine anyway.
a_eliza.long: It only asked questions back, by rule, and people projected feeling onto it all the same — the ELIZA effect. It was the first experiment to show how readily humans make a machine into a person.
a_eliza.cause: After Dartmouth, attempts to handle language kept coming.
a_eliza.effect: Fifty-six years later ChatGPT made that dream of conversation real.

a_expert.title: Expert systems
a_expert.body: Expert systems, which moved specialist knowledge into if-then rules, flourished commercially. It was AI's first industrialisation.
a_expert.long: Systems such as MYCIN (infectious disease) and XCON (order configuration) went into real work, and AI earned money for the first time. But as the rules multiplied, maintenance collapsed, and the field headed into a second winter.
a_expert.cause: Symbolic AI aimed at practical use by encoding expert knowledge.
a_expert.effect: Its limits raised the value of a neural network that learns from data.

a_lstm.title: LSTM
a_lstm.body: Hochreiter and Schmidhuber proposed the LSTM, which holds long context in memory. It opened the way for sequence data such as speech and translation.
a_lstm.long: Where earlier recurrent networks forgot the distant past, the LSTM held onto it with gates. It is the structure that carried translation and speech recognition through the 2010s.
a_lstm.cause: Language and speech needed a structure that could remember order in time.
a_lstm.effect: The Transformer's attention would later leap past that limit by a wide margin.

a_imagenet.title: ImageNet
a_imagenet.sub: The data that opened its eyes
a_imagenet.body: Fei-Fei Li built ImageNet, 14 million labelled images. It was a change of mind: not the algorithm, the data.
a_imagenet.long: Fourteen million images across some twenty thousand categories laid out the field on which deep learning could grow. Its annual recognition contest became AlexNet's stage.
a_imagenet.cause: The bottleneck was not the model but the absence of enough data.
a_imagenet.effect: Three years later AlexNet used this data to prove deep learning.

a_gan.title: GANs
a_gan.body: Goodfellow's GAN set a generator against a discriminator to make images that look real. It is the direct ancestor of generative AI.
a_gan.long: Two networks compete like a forger and an authenticator, shaping results that grow steadily more convincing. It opened the age of generation, from deepfakes to art.
a_gan.cause: There was strong appetite for AI that creates rather than only recognises.
a_gan.effect: Eight years later it led to the public explosion of the generative AI boom.

a_gpt4.title: GPT-4
a_gpt4.body: A multimodal model arrived that understands images as well as text. It passed a range of professional exams and set a new bar for reasoning.
a_gpt4.long: GPT-4 read images, handled complex reasoning and coding, and passed many human examinations. It raised the level of trust placed in AI as a general assistant.
a_gpt4.cause: ChatGPT's success pulled out a larger and smarter model.
a_gpt4.effect: It became the stepping stone toward the age of tool-holding agents.

a_claude.title: Claude
a_claude.body: Anthropic released Claude, an AI shaped by constitutional principles to be helpful, honest, and harmless. It settled in as an assistant that reads long documents whole and answers with care.
a_claude.long: Claude was trained with constitutional AI — refining itself against a set of principles rather than being corrected item by item. It reads long documents whole and answers carefully, which earned it trust as an assistant for real work.
a_claude.cause: The more capable the model, the more its safe shaping became the central task.
a_claude.effect: Safety and trust are the precondition for a second brain you would hand your own data to.

a_gemini.title: Gemini
a_gemini.body: Google DeepMind presented Gemini, which handles text, images, audio, and code as one body. Woven into Search and Android, it became an everyday tool for billions.
a_gemini.long: Gemini was designed to handle text, images, audio, and code in a single model from the start, rather than bolting them together. Tied into Google Search, Android, and Workspace, it worked its way into the daily life of billions.
a_gemini.cause: The search empire answered the shock of ChatGPT head on.
a_gemini.effect: Competition between giant models made an AI assistant everyone's default tool.

a_harness.title: Harness engineering
a_harness.sub: Wrapping a model so it can work
a_harness.body: Designing what surrounds the model — tools, context, evaluation, orchestration — rose above the model itself. The same model gets far smarter when it is dressed well.
a_harness.long: With the same model, performance diverges sharply depending on which tools it is handed, what goes into its context, and how it is evaluated and corrected. Designing that harness around the model became an engineering discipline of its own.
a_harness.cause: Making the model bigger and nothing else had reached its limit.
a_harness.effect: What you hand an agent, and how, is what separates one from another.

a_robot.title: AI robots and humanoids
a_robot.body: Action models that see (vision), understand (language), and move (action) rode onto humanoids. Embodied AI that helps people in factories and logistics went on trial.
a_robot.long: Vision-language-action models that see, understand speech, and move were loaded onto humanoids, and AI stepped off the screen into physical work. Walking, gripping, and carrying were solved quickly.
a_robot.cause: The reasoning of language models meshed with robot control.
a_robot.effect: Embodied AI pulled the debate over jobs and safety into the physical present.

a_local.title: Local and on-device AI
a_local.sub: AI running in your own hand
a_local.body: Open-weight models met light inference engines, and AI began running on laptops and phones without the cloud. A privacy-first path opened: your data stays on your device.
a_local.long: Open-weight models such as Meta's LLaMA met light inference engines like llama.cpp and Ollama, and capable AI came to run on a personal device with no cloud at all. The path opened for keeping your data on your own machine.
a_local.cause: Cost and privacy concerns about huge cloud models kept growing.
a_local.effect: It became the foundation for an on-device personal AI — a second brain.

w_nvidia.title: The AI chip boom
w_nvidia.body: Demand for GPUs to train and run AI exploded, and NVIDIA rose to the rank of the world's most valuable companies. It became clear that competing in AI means competing for computation.
w_nvidia.long: Demand for the GPUs used to train and run AI exploded, and NVIDIA's value climbed astronomically. Who holds more computation became the measure of power in AI.
w_nvidia.cause: Competition between giant models absorbed enormous computation.
w_nvidia.effect: Chips, electricity, and data centres became the bottleneck of the AI age.

w_aimna.title: AI megadeals and the race for capital
w_aimna.body: Big tech invested tens of billions in AI companies, and acquisitions of talent and startups followed one after another. AI became a field of capital redrawing the industrial map.
w_aimna.long: As with Microsoft's investment in OpenAI, big tech poured tens of billions into AI companies and talent, and acquisitions followed one after another. AI became the ground on which capital and industry were redrawn.
w_aimna.cause: AI emerged as the technology that would decide the next decade.
w_aimna.effect: A structure hardened in which power gathers into a few very large companies.

w_robotnews.title: Robots go commercial
w_robotnews.body: Humanoids entering factories, self-driving cars, and delivery robots filled the headlines. AI walked out of the screen and into the physical world.
w_robotnews.long: Humanoids entering factories, robotaxis, and delivery robots filled the headlines. Cleverness on a screen spread into moving AI on streets and factory floors.
w_robotnews.cause: AI's intelligence ripened enough to start looking for a body.
w_robotnews.effect: AI entered the stage of changing the physical surroundings of daily life.
